To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure and composition of the submandibular gland sialolith resected using laser were similar to that of dentine.
the resected sialolith is composed of inorganic and organic constituents and its structure is similar to that in dentine.
the structure of sialolith is like that of the dentin part of human teeth, and the formation of the sialith may be due to the high content of calcium and phosphorous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of sialolith resected by Nd:YAG (1,064 nm) laser.
the analysis of the chemical structure of a resected sialolith.
the structural characterization of sialolith by spectroscopic and thermal analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resected sialolith is a mixture of inorganic calcium phosphate, proteinaceous organic matter, and other organic molecules.
the sialolith resected using laser is similar to dentine and the in situ disintegration of sialolith may involve very high temperatures.
the inorganic part is the major constituent of the sialith and it is a mixture of apatitic and calcium oxalate phases with the presence of organic matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sialolith observed here is a mixture of inorganic (hydroxyapatite) and organic (proteins and amino acids) components and the inorganic part is the major component.

the inorganic component of sialolith is calcium phosphate, and the organic component is mainly proteinaceous in nature, which may be due to the endogenous proteins and amino acids of saliva and/or food.
sialoliths are formed due to the precipitation of calcium phosphate salts in the ducts of the salivary glands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sialoliths can be resected using laser.
the resection of a sialolith using an Nd: YAG laser is possible.
the resected sample is a mixture of the inorganic and organic components.
